protocol.name: trindle_own_press_v1

description.summary: which presses the person made themselves

protocol.description:
Trindle's compositor tells a program which of the keys, clicks and touches it is passed were made by the person on a real device, as against a made-up mouse or keyboard. A program binds the global and is then sent an event before each such press, on the same connection, so the event is always there before the press it speaks of. Nothing is sent for any other press: "not the person's" is the rule.
Offered only to programs outside every box.

interface.name: trindle_own_press_v1

description.summary: the person's own presses, named as they are made

interface.description: For as long as this object lives, the compositor names each press the person made that it passes to this program.

event.name: own

description.summary: the press with this number is the person's own

event.description: Sent just before a key, a pointer button or a touch is passed to a surface of this program, when the person made it. The serial is the one that press carries, going down or coming up.

event.name: refused

description.summary: a press that was not the person's was kept from this surface

event.description: Sent when the compositor kept a made-up key, click or touch back from this surface of the program: a question only the person may answer was out, or the surface is one only the person may press. The program says why where the person is working. Sent at most once a second to a program.

arg.name: surface
arg.summary: the surface the press was kept from

event.name: was

description.summary: the key really pressed behind a changed one

event.description: Sent just before a key or a pointer button is passed to a surface of this program, when the person's own change of keys and buttons made it from another: the code is the kernel's number for the key or button really pressed. Sent whoever made the press; it says nothing of whose it was.

arg.name: code
arg.summary: the key or button really pressed
